baseDescription:
upscale_video performs promptless, deterministic video super-resolution of exactly one uploaded
or generated video. RelayVSR is recommended for new upscales. Use it when the user asks to upscale,
enlarge, sharpen, or increase the resolution of an existing video, or wants a 1080p, 1440p, 2K, 4K, or HD
copy of it. The output keeps every source frame, the exact frame rate, the full aspect ratio, and
the original audio.

Do not invent a prompt and do not route a pure video upscale through video_to_video,
generate_video, extend_video, or replace_video_segment; those tools re-render or edit content.
Use video_to_video only when the user explicitly names a generative model such as Seedance for
the re-render. Do not use upscale_image for videos.

Omit sourceVideoIndex to use the latest generated video, falling back to the most recent upload.
Use zero-based non-negative indices for generated videos; -1 selects the first uploaded video
and -2 the second. targetResolution is the output short edge: omit it for 1440p (or 1080p when
the source is too small for 1440p), and set 1080 when the user asks for 1080p or Full HD.

Explicitly set model to relayvsr for new upscales. Use flashvsr when the user requests FlashVSR
or specifically wants its detailPreference, processingSpeed or seed controls. Omitted model
retains FlashVSR for compatibility. Set targetResolution to 2160 for 4K or 2160p; 2160 is valid
only with relayvsr.

With FlashVSR the output is at most twice the source size, so 1440p needs a source short edge of
720-768px and 1080p needs 540-768px, and sources must be at most about 1344x768 pixels (768x1344
in portrait). FlashVSR cannot produce 4K or any size above 1440p, so a 4K request always uses
relayvsr.

With RelayVSR the output is at most twice the source size for a source up to 1920x1080 pixels
(1080x1920 in portrait), or four times for a source up to 1344x768 (768x1344 in portrait), so 2160p
needs a source short edge of 540-768px or exactly 1080px, and the output's long edge can be at
most 3840px. Nothing here produces a size above 2160p: when the user asks for one, say so and offer
2160p instead of silently delivering less.

Sources must also be 1-60 fps and 100 MB. The server sets the maximum clip length and rejects a
source that is too long; never quote a length limit yourself. If the tool reports that the source
is too long or outside these limits, relay that error to the user instead of switching to a
generative video tool.

When using FlashVSR, its default recipe favors temporal stability. Set detailPreference to sharper only when the
user asks for a sharper, crisper, or more detailed upscale, and processingSpeed to faster only
when they ask for a quicker one. Leave seed out unless the user gives a seed or asks for a
different or random variation (-1 is random). None of these options changes the price. RelayVSR
refuses all three: leave them out with model relayvsr.

parameterDocs.sourceVideoIndex: Omit for the latest generated video, then the most recent upload. Generated videos are zero-based; -1/-2 select uploaded videos.
parameterDocs.model: Explicitly set relayvsr for new upscales. Use flashvsr when requested or for its detailPreference, processingSpeed or seed controls. Omitted model retains FlashVSR for compatibility.
parameterDocs.targetResolution: Output short edge in pixels: 2160 (relayvsr only), 1440, or 1080. Omit for the default (1440, or 1080 for sources too small for it); set 1080 when the user asks for 1080p or Full HD, and 2160 with relayvsr for 4K or 2160p.
parameterDocs.detailPreference: FlashVSR only. stable (default) or sharper. Set sharper only when the user asks for a sharper, crisper, or more detailed result.
parameterDocs.processingSpeed: FlashVSR only. stable (default) or faster. Set faster only when the user asks for a quicker upscale.
parameterDocs.seed: FlashVSR only. Omit for the repeatable default 0. -1 is random; otherwise an integer 0-4294967295 the user gave.
